title: fix(app-shell): the Debug run leaves every node and gates screen fields the way the runtime does, and keeps unmodelled tokens as written (objectui#10692)
body:
Fixes #10692
Clause-②: no — the Studio Debug run's routing and screen gating begin matching the runtime; no export, schema or accept set moves

Family closure card: objectui#10693 (a screen field's `visibleWhen` failing open on the legacy evaluator) and objectui#10695 (an embedded unmodelled token rendering as an empty string) were folded into this card by triage, and this PR carries their rows. Serial after objectui#10615 (PR objectui#10672, merged as `383a34f5`), which this branch is based on.

## What this changes

**Successor selection** (`flow-simulator.ts`). Every node now leaves through one path, `FlowSimulator.route`, which follows the runtime's `traverseNext`: a `fault` edge is never a successor; an out-edge with a `condition` is guarded, `isDefault` or not (the condition wins); an `isDefault` edge with no condition is taken only when no guard was true; every other out-edge is always taken; nothing taken ends the branch with no error. A decision that declares `config.conditions` reports the first true entry's `label` as its branch (else `default`), which narrows its out-edges the way the runtime's `decision` executor plus `traverseNext` narrow them; `default` is also claimed by the `isDefault` edge; when nothing claims the branch every out-edge is considered and the step says so. An approval resumed with a decision goes through the same path. `enqueueSuccessors` and the decision-only routing are gone. Kept as ruled: when several guards are true the Debug run takes the first (objectstack#15429 pending).

**Screen field `visibleWhen`** (`flow-sim-validate.ts`, `screen-spec.ts`). `isFieldVisibleWhen` goes through `evalVisibleWhen`, which shares `evalCelPredicate` with `evalGuard` and the new `evalBranchPredicate`: one CEL call (`@objectstack/formula`'s `ExpressionEngine` over `flowCelScope`) for every predicate in the simulator. A predicate that is refused (a `{var}` brace, a non-string) or faults (a variable that is not set, a CEL error) reads as HIDDEN, and the Debug run's screen pause names each field hidden that way with the error. `evalCondition` (the legacy `@object-ui/core` `ExpressionEvaluator` path) had no importer left and is retired.

**Template tokens** (`flow-simulator.ts` `interpolateString`). A token the Debug run does not model (`NOW()` / `TODAY()`, `$User.*`, function calls, arithmetic) is kept as written inside a longer string, as a whole-token one already was, and the assignment step names each one. A call to a function the runtime does not know fails the node at runtime; the Debug run keeps it and runs on. This is the triage's first option; the pure tokens are not modelled because `NOW()` / `TODAY()` are clock-dependent, `$User.*` needs a run context the designer has none of, and the runtime's arithmetic is a `Function()`-evaluated dialect that is not cheap to reproduce faithfully.

**Timeline** (`FlowSimulatorPanel.tsx`, one line, outside the claim's three files and declared here). Successor selection now lists every out-edge it considered, and an unguarded one has no condition text, so its row was blank; it reads the arrow and its target. One panel pin.

## Runtime rules the pins are written against

Read at objectstack `origin/main` `16c5a33fd`: `AutomationEngine.traverseNext`, `evaluateCondition` and `refuseInvalidScreenInput` (`engine.ts`), the `decision` executor (`builtin/logic-nodes.ts`), `validateScreenInputs` (`screen-input-contract.ts`), `interpolateString` / `resolveToken` (`builtin/template.ts`); and in this repo `visibleScreenFields` (`ScreenView.tsx`). The runtime itself was not executed.

| Node kind | Out-edge | `traverseNext` | Debug run at this head |
|---|---|---|---|
| any (the rule has no per-type arm) | `type: 'fault'` | filtered out before bucketing | never a successor |
| any | has `condition` (with or without `isDefault`) | conditional bucket: evaluated in declared order; every true one runs its target; a false one records `skipped` | guarded; the first true one is taken (first-true kept as ruled) |
| any | no `condition`, `isDefault` | default bucket: taken only when no conditional edge matched | same |
| any | no `condition`, not default | unconditional bucket: always taken | same (the card's divergence 1: it used to be "Branch has no condition." and not taken) |
| any | nothing taken | the branch ends, no error | same (it used to fail the run with "No branch matched") |
| any | a guard faults | `evaluateCondition` throws after the node ran; the run fails | the step is an error and the run stops there (the card's divergence 2: a non-decision's guard used to be ignored) |
| any | a guard is refused (shape, blank, dialect, parse) | refused at `registerFlow`; the flow never runs | the step is an error and the run stops there |
| decision with `config.conditions` | branch = first true entry's `label`, else `default` | narrows to out-edges whose `label` equals the branch; `default` is also claimed by `isDefault` edges; no claimant: warn and consider every out-edge | same, and the step says when nothing claims the branch (used to ignore `config.conditions`) |
| decision without `config.conditions` | no branch | a plain gateway: out-edges alone | same |
| approval, resumed | branch = the decision's label | same narrowing | same, except the label is matched case-insensitively (note 3) |

Multi-match (PR objectui#10672 Acceptance note 4): the runtime takes every true guard, and a later fault fails the run after the earlier true branch ran; the Debug run takes the first and, on a fault, stops before any branch runs. Both are kept as ruled and stated on the step. `isDefault` plus `condition` (note 6): the condition wins in both.

| Screen field `visibleWhen` | server (`refuseInvalidScreenInput`, `validateScreenInputs`) | client (`visibleScreenFields`) | Debug run at this head |
|---|---|---|---|
| engine and scope | `evaluateCondition`: CEL over the run's variables plus the submitted bag; `Boolean(value)` | `@objectstack/formula` through `evalFieldPredicate`, over the screen's own field names plus collected values; `value === true` | the guards' CEL call over the run's variables (`flowCelScope`); `Boolean(value)` |
| absent or blank | absent: unconditional; blank: refused at `registerFlow` on main | shown | shown |
| evaluates to false (`size(tags) > 0` with `tags = []`, `vars.n == 2` with `n = 3`) | hidden | `tags` / `vars` are not screen fields: faults, fails open, shown | hidden |
| faults (a variable that is not set, a CEL error) | treated as hidden: `required` is not enforced, a warning is logged | fails open (shown), one warning | hidden, and the screen step names the field and the error |
| refused (a `{var}` brace, a non-string) | `registerFlow` refuses the flow | n/a | hidden, named on the step |

The Debug run takes the server's reading, per the triage ("a stated reading instead of failing open"). The client's fail-open and its screen-only scope are a divergence inside the runtime itself, measured and reported below, not resolved here.

| Template token | runtime `interpolateString` | Debug run at this head |
|---|---|---|
| `'{who}'`, `'hi {who}'`, dotted paths, indices, nested values | the variable's value, as PR objectui#10672 modelled it | same |
| `'{NOW()}'` (whole) | a timestamp | kept as written, named on the step (was kept, unnamed) |
| `'at {NOW()}'`, `'to {$User.Email}'`, `'v={n + 1}'` (embedded) | the value inside the text | kept as written, named on the step (was an empty string) |

## Acceptance notes

Observed, not handled here.

1. Client and server disagree on a screen field's `visibleWhen` (measured; see the report's findings): `visibleScreenFields` in `ScreenView.tsx` evaluates it over the screen's own field names only and fails open on a fault, while `refuseInvalidScreenInput` evaluates it over the run's variables and treats a fault as hidden. A predicate over a flow variable (`vars.n == 2`, `n == 2`, `size(tags) > 0`) is therefore shown by the client and, when the field is `required`, its `required` is not enforced by the server. Probe (a temporary test, not committed): `visibleScreenFields` over four such predicates with no values returned all four fields. Filed by the seat as objectui#10743.
2. Multi-match: the runtime takes every true guard and fails after an earlier true branch ran when a later guard faults; the Debug run takes the first and stops before any branch runs. Kept as ruled (objectstack#15429 pending) and stated on the step.
3. An approval's decision label is matched case-insensitively by the Debug run (`Approve` claims `approve`), a pre-existing leniency; the runtime's `traverseNext` matches `label` exactly, and with no exact claimant it considers every out-edge. Not measured against the runtime here.
4. A non-string `visibleWhen` (a boolean) is refused by `registerFlow`, so the runtime never runs the flow; the server's own evaluator would otherwise stringify it. The Debug run refuses it and hides the field, naming the refusal, rather than refusing the whole run at preflight.
5. Fault edges stay out of scope, as objectui#10615 recorded: a node that fails stops the Debug run, and a `fault` edge is only ever excluded from successor selection.
